sections.h2: Where is Lowell, Massachusetts, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Lowell is a city in Middlesex County at the meeting of the Merrimack and Concord rivers, and it shares the title of traditional county seat with Cambridge. The 2020 census counted 115,554 residents, which made it the fifth most populous city in the state and the third largest in the Boston metropolitan area.

The city covers 14.5 square miles, with about 0.8 square miles of that water. Lowell was settled in 1652, incorporated as a town in 1826 and became a city in 1836. It carries the name of Francis Cabot Lowell, a figure of the Industrial Revolution.

Lowell uses a city manager and city council form of government, and it has five ZIP codes, one of which (01853) is for post office boxes only.

sections.h2: How did mills and canals shape Lowell?
sections.html:
The Pawtucket Falls gave Lowell its power. Native people fished at the falls for centuries before the mills, and in the 1800s the falls drove the textile factories that made Lowell the cradle of the American Industrial Revolution.

Much of the old mill district is now preserved as Lowell National Historical Park, run by the National Park Service.

Lowell also took in refugees during the Cambodian genocide of 1975 to 1979. The city has a Cambodia Town and the second-largest Cambodian-American population in the country, according to Wikipedia.

Lowell has eight distinct neighborhoods, and each has its own character and ZIP code grouping. Knowing which one you are in helps frame what buyers expect.

  • The Highlands (01851): the most populated area, with almost a quarter of residents. It lies in the southwest and includes Tyler Park, Drum Hill and the UMass Lowell South Campus.
  • Centralville (01850): the northeastern section north of the Merrimack River, including Christian Hill.
  • Downtown, Belvidere, Back Central and South Lowell (01852): the southeastern sections. Belvidere is mostly residential, and the Belvidere Hill Historic District runs along Fairmount Street.
  • The Acre and Pawtucketville: the remaining two of the eight neighborhoods. Ask which one a property sits in before comparing it with others.

Smaller names such as Ayers City, Bleachery, Chapel Hill, the Grove, Oaklands and Swede Village are still used, and Wikipedia notes that people are using them again.

sections.h2: What does the Lowell climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Lowell has long cold winters and hot humid summers. The yearly average temperature is 49 degrees, and January highs average around 34 degrees in the 1991 to 2020 normals.

Snow is the main factor. Lowell averages about 56 inches a season, and the heaviest season on record brought 120 inches in the winter of 2014 and 2015. That kind of load tests older roofs, porches and gutters.

If you are selling a house with a patched roof, ice damage or an old boiler, a buyer's inspector will flag it. A cash buyer will usually price those items in directly instead of asking you to fix them first.

sections.h2: Who works in Lowell, and how do residents commute?
sections.html:
Higher education is a major presence. UMass Lowell has three campuses in the city, and Middlesex Community College has campuses in Lowell and Bedford, together serving more than 31,000 students according to Wikipedia. Lowell General Hospital and Saints Medical Center add health care jobs.

Roads include Interstate 495, U.S. Route 3, the Lowell Connector and Massachusetts Routes 3A, 38, 110, 113 and 133. The Lowell Regional Transit Authority runs local buses, and the MBTA Lowell Line has several daily trips to North Station.

Lowell Public Schools runs the public schools, and Lowell High School is the district high school. Greater Lowell Technical High School and several charter schools also serve students.

sections.h2: How do Lowell property taxes work, and what if I fall behind?
sections.html:
Lowell bills real estate tax in four installments, issued July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1. Due dates are the first of August, November, February and May, or the first business day of the month.

If you do not pay by the due date, interest runs at 14 percent a year. A $30 demand fee and demand notice follow after May 1, and unpaid real estate tax can become a lien. If your mortgage company escrows your taxes, you are still responsible for making sure the bill is paid.

For questions about why a bill is high, the Treasurer points people to the Assessor's office. Online card payments carry a fee of at least 2.95 percent, with a $1 minimum, and e-check payments cost $0.40.

sections.h2: Can I challenge my Lowell assessment?
sections.html:
Yes, but you must follow a fixed schedule. Under the Appellate Tax Board's guide, an abatement application is due by the first installment due date of the actual tax bill, generally February 1 for a quarterly-billing city.

Assessors have three months to act. If they do not, the application is treated as denied and you have three months to file with the board. You must pay each installment on time for the board to hear your case, with narrow exceptions such as a tax of $5,000 or less.

The value is measured as of January 1 before the fiscal year, so recent sales of similar homes near that date are your best evidence.

sections.h2: What does a Lowell closing involve, and who buys as-is?
sections.html:
Attorneys handle Massachusetts closings, and your deed will be recorded at the Middlesex County registry. The fire department must issue a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate of compliance, and the state advises booking the inspection once you have a closing date.

The statute on deed excise lists $2 for each $500 of the price, so confirm the total at the registry. You also need payoff letters for any mortgage and a clear tax and water balance.

The state's law library explains that most Massachusetts land is recorded land, filed at the Registry of Deeds with a book and page number. A smaller share is registered land, described on a Certificate of Title issued by the Land Court. Your attorney will check which system applies to your lot, since registered land follows slightly different filing steps.

Owners who sell to us often have an inherited house, a mill-era multi-family building that needs systems work, or a property with delinquent taxes. We make an offer on the condition as found, and you decide whether it beats listing.

faqs.q: When are Lowell real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due August 1, November 1, February 1 and May 1, or the first business day of that month. Bills are issued July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on late Lowell property taxes?
faqs.a: Late real estate tax in Lowell accrues interest at 14 percent a year. After the May 1 due date, a $30 demand fee is added, and a demand notice is mailed for any unpaid bill.

faqs.q: Is the postmark date accepted for a Lowell tax payment?
faqs.a: No. The city says a payment counts when the Treasurer's office receives it, so mail early or pay online. Rejected online payments can take up to three business days to become available again.
Lowell is in Middlesex County, so deeds are recorded through the county Registry of Deeds. You can search a deed copy at masslandrecords.com, which the state law library points to.

faqs.q: Does Lowell require a smoke and CO certificate when selling?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department for smoke and carbon monoxide alarms when a home is sold. The fire department charges a fee.
